definition: BERT's subword algorithm, similar to BPE but choosing merges by likelihood gain rather than raw frequency.
details: BERT's subword algorithm, similar to BPE but choosing merges by likelihood gain rather than raw frequency.

explainer.lead: WordPiece is BERT's subword algorithm, which splits text into frequent word pieces. It matters because subword tokenization lets models handle rare and unseen words.

tiers.eli5: Long or rare words get chopped into smaller familiar chunks, like building 'unhappiness' from pieces it already knows.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on WordPiece to keep vocabulary size manageable while covering unseen words; a pitfall is choosing merge order, which here follows likelihood gain rather than frequency.
tiers.paperLevel: A subword algorithm similar to BPE, but merges are chosen by likelihood gain rather than raw frequency; it is the subword algorithm used by BERT.

explainer.example: A rare word absent from the vocabulary is split into a small set of WordPiece chunks the model does know.
